newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak IRB shares a speculative buy - ING.
newsitem.headline: Slovak IRB shares a speculative buy - ING.

text.p: Shares of Investicna a Rozvojova Banka a.s. (IRB), Slovakia's third largest commercial bank, are a speculative buy, an October investment report by ING Barings said.

It said the quality of IRB's loan portfolio, with a high share of classified loans, has improved "significantly" due to a restructuring of the bank's debt funding for the controversial Mochovce nuclear power plant in Slovakia.
"We are impressed with the quality of the management and believe that IRB has a potential to gain greater loan market share and reduce funding costs over the medium term," the report said.
IRB's assets totalled 48.23 as of the end of 1995, of which 36.9 billion were extended loans. The bank's capital adequacy ratio hit 7.25 percent in the end of 1995.
However, the report added: "The major risk faced by investors is the presence of Slovak steel giant VSZ and allied companies as shareholders in the bank".
As of July 31, VSZ held 14.63 percent in IRB.
The central bank recently rejected a request by VSZ to increase its holdings in the bank.
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
The state holds a 35 percent stake in IRB through its privatisation agency the National Property Fund (NPF).
